newsitem.title: JAPAN: Caution over Japan stocks may be corrected--Utsumi.
newsitem.headline: Caution over Japan stocks may be corrected--Utsumi.

text.p: Japanese equity markets could see a shift of money into stocks by institutional investors, a former Japanese Finance Ministry official said on Tuesday.
"The shift towards the Japanese stock market is a possibility," Makoto Utsumi, a former Japanese vice finance minister, told Reuters Financial Television (RFTV).
Utsumi noted that strength in U.S. and European equity markets had come amid weakness in European economic fundamentals and turmoil in Asian markets.

Utsumi, who is now a business professor at Keio University in Tokyo, told RFTV that, given these conditions, he did not understand why Japanese investors were so "excessively cautious" about putting money into Japanese equities, but added that sooner or later there would be a correction to this situation that would see funds flowing towards stocks.

"You know the New York stock prices and, though with very recessionary situations in Europe with a very high unemployment ratio, their stock markets are performing very well," Utsumi said in the interview.

"And on the other hand, investors are withdrawing money from other Asian markets, so I don't see the reason why investors, especially Japanese investors, are so excessively cautious of putting their money in stocks."
He continued: "But sooner or later I think there would also be a correction."
Utsumi would not comment on the extent of the correction to stock price levels.
